claims.says: For a separable sub-plan, batched Apply (run once over the tagged batch, outputs merged back by origin) returns exactly the per-row Apply rows, in the same order.
For a separable sub-plan, batched Optional returns the same rows with the same multiplicities as per-row Optional, though possibly in a different order.
For a separable sub-plan, batched SemiApply and anti-SemiApply keep exactly the input rows for which the sub-plan has (or has no) result, in input order.
MERGE without SET, off the all-bound path, from a consistent cache, ends with the same graph, next id and emitted rows as per-row openCypher MERGE, however the rows are split into batches.
If the body never errors, a fresh FOREACH over any input batches passes every row through in order, in non-empty batches of at most B rows, and runs the body on exactly each row's items.
